findings.text: Scratch setup (`copytree`, `makedirs`, and the `open` inside `put`) can raise `OSError` (permissions, disk full, `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup). `run` only catches `Refused`/`Unverifiable`, so those escape as a raw traceback rather than the documented clean refusal/UNVERIFIABLE that writes nothing. Wrap the scratch build (and `put`) in `try/except OSError` and raise `Unverifiable`.
findings.title: bug

findings.text:
This folds a tri-state `pins_hold` result into a refusal: an `unverifiable` outcome becomes exit 1 ("pins do not
hold") instead of exit 3, contradicting the tool's own three-state contract (`docs/claim-format.md`, AGENTS.md).
Split `fail` (Refused, exit 1) from any non-`pass`/non-`fail` outcome (Unverifiable, exit 3).
findings.title: Report unverifiable pins as exit 3
findings.code:
if policy.get("outcome") != "pass":
    details = "\n".join(f"  {d}" for d in policy.get("details") or []) or "  (no details)"
    raise Refused(f"the migrated pins do not hold (`pins_hold` is {policy.get('outcome')!r}); "
                  f"re-word the statement or fix the authored slot, never edit a pin to fit "
                  f"the parse:\n{details}")

findings.text: `run_req` runs an arbitrary `req` found on `PATH` with no `timeout`, and `capture_output=True` buffers unbounded output. A hung `canon`/`gate` (or a corpus large enough to stall the pipe) blocks the migration forever, with no way to tell it apart from a slow run. Pass a `timeout=` and translate `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (and `UnicodeDecodeError` from `text=True`) into `Unverifiable`, so the tool still exits 3 with "nothing written".
findings.title: bug

findings.text:
When `planned` is empty (e.g. an empty or already-processed `claims/`), this still demands `req` on `PATH` and
runs `canon`/`gate` over an empty scratch corpus, so a true no-op can exit 3 or spuriously refuse. Guard the
verification on `planned` and change the waiver `else` to an explicit `elif not verify:` so an empty verified run
does not print "NOT VERIFIED".
findings.title: Skip verification for empty migration

findings.text:
`pins_hold` is tri-state (PASS / FAIL / UNVERIFIABLE), but this branch folds every
non-`pass` outcome into a refusal: when the gate returns `unverifiable` (e.g. a degraded
registry, or a pin it cannot judge), the tool prints "the migrated pins do not hold
(`pins_hold` is 'unverifiable')" and exits 1, instead of reporting UNVERIFIABLE and
exiting 3 as the tool's own documented exit contract promises. The pins were not
refuted—they could not be judged—so an adopter is told their content contradicts its
statement when the environment merely cannot check it. The same conflation applies to a
non-zero `req canon`, which is wrapped as a refusal, so a garbled/incompatible `req` is
reported as an invalid file rather than an unprovable one. What I could not verify from
the diff is whether `pins_hold` can actually return `unverifiable` while `req canon`
exits 0; if it can, this branch should distinguish `fail` from `unverifiable` and map the
latter to exit 3.
findings.title: Tri-state conflation

findings.text: This test can pass for the wrong reason. The migrator refuses with exit 1 not only when `pins_hold` flags the contradiction, but also via the `judged < expected` guard ("only N of M migrated pin(s) were judged") when `without_applicability` fails to make the claim apply. A regression in that stripping (the exact behavior this test is meant to pin) would still leave exit 1 and an unchanged snapshot, so the stated property ("the contradiction is found despite the selector") is not actually asserted. Pin the failure's identity the way test (b) does.
findings.title: test

findings.text: Every "nothing written" proof (tests b, c, d, e) uses a single-file corpus, so the multi-file path is never exercised. The tool currently verifies all planned files in one scratch copy before writing any, which is what makes a refused mixed corpus leave `claims/` untouched; but a regression to per-file verify-and-write would still pass every existing test (the one good file is written, then the bad one aborts). Add a fixture with one valid and one contradicted claim and assert exit 1 plus a whole-directory unchanged snapshot — that is the case that distinguishes the two designs (and the duplicate-name refusal in `verify_output`).
findings.title: test
